ak_eyes_of_the_world.blurb: A small, little-developed bolted cliff in the Tee Harbor zone of Juneau, on the slope above the Tee Harbor boulder field. Five sport climbs are on record, mostly around 5.9 with one easier line and one 5.11. The cliff top sits near 1,050 feet, and the view from up there gives the place its name. The rock is solid and looks like the same stone as the boulders below. This is not a roadside crag: there is no path to the base, so you climb down by rope from the rim and climb back up. Expect a quiet, adventurous outing rather than a polished sport venue.
ak_eyes_of_the_world.approach: A faint, brushy, poorly marked trail starts across from the pullout and climbs through alders to the top of the cliff. There is no trail to the base of the routes.

ak_nugget_boulder.blurb: A single granite block of roughly 30 feet in the Lower Reed Valley, part of the Hatcher Pass climbing zone in Southcentral Alaska. Five climbs are recorded, running from about 5.6 up to 5.11, and they mix trad, bolted and top-rope lines. The rock quality is rated excellent. Most lines are short and approachable, so it works as a quick warm-up stop or a place to introduce newer climbers to roped climbing. It stands across the stream from the Snowbird Slab, and the walk in follows the Reed Lakes trail past old mine remains. Top anchors allow a rappel or walk-off.

ak_birds_of_prey.blurb: A quiet wall in the Reed Lakes basin of Hatcher Pass, reached on foot along the Reed Lakes trail. Five roped climbs are on record, all between about 5.8 and 5.10, with a good mix of trad, bolted and top-rope options. The golden stone catches sun for most of the day and dries fast after rain. It sees little traffic, which makes it a pleasant, uncrowded day of mid-grade cragging for a party comfortable with a gully scramble and a stream crossing to get to the base.
